text:
Alex: Heads-up — trying to provision a small H100 burst pool in eu-west3 for the new low-latency embedding pipeline. Hitting quota and cluster-autoscaler is spinning up nodes then deleting them immediately. Anyone awake?

Maria: Are you seeing a quota error or CA just not attaching pods? Paste the error or logs.

Alex: Getting QUOTA_EXCEEDED on 'accelerators' when creating the nodepool, then CA logs: "NoScaleUpRequests: no nodes can satisfy pod resource requests" even though we created a node pool.

Rashid: Two separate things likely: 1) GCP quota for H100 in eu-west3 (we hit soft limit), and 2) mismatch between node labels/taints and pod tolerations so CA thinks nodes aren't usable.

Maria: Can you paste the pool create command you used? Also which KSA / node pool service account? If it's using default SA without proper scopes the GPU drivers/daemonset might fail to register.

Alex: Command I used: 
```
gcloud container node-pools create h100-burst-1 \
  --cluster=redwood-prod-eu \
  --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-h100,count=1 \
  --num-nodes=0 \
  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=6 \
  --node-taints=dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule \
  --node-labels=pool=gpu,hw=h100 
```
Pods set nodeSelector to pool=gpu and toleration for dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule.

Sophie: Quick note on networking — eu-west3 subnets we're using require a NAT gateway for nodes that pull images from GCR. If the node can't pull the gpu-driver daemonset image it will never become Ready and CA will scale it down. Check egress/NAT and private clusters config.

Rashid: Also check the GPU plugin daemonset logs. If nvidia-driver-install or device-plugin crashes the node will taint NotReady and CA will remove. Run: `kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nvidia-driver-installer`

Maria: For quota, open a GCP support quota increase and we can also fallback to A10G for short term if H100 is blocked. H100 quota is limited in a lot of EU zones.

Alex: Ok created a quota ticket but want to avoid A10G perf regressions for the embed latency SLA. Any suggestions for autoscaler settings to avoid flapping?

Rashid: Recommended config: use CA expander=least-waste (or priority) so it picks nodes that minimize waste; set scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m to avoid immediate tear-down; set balance-similar-node-groups=true if mixing instance types. Example CA flags: `--expander=least-waste --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m --balance-similar-node-groups=true`.

Rashid: Also use nodeAffinity + taints + priorityClass for production GPU pods. Example pod snippet: 
```yaml
spec:
  priorityClassName: gpu-critical
  tolerations:
  - key: "dedicated"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "gpu"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: "hw"
            operator: "In"
            values: ["h100"]
```
This prevents casual dev jobs from landing on the H100 pool.

Sophie: Also consider two-tier approach: create a small dedicated reserved pool (1-2 nodes) for latency-critical traffic and a separate burst autoscaling pool with preemptible/spot nodes for warmup and scale. That keeps costs down while guaranteeing minimal capacity.

Maria: Cost quick numbers: H100 on-demand in cloud is roughly ~3-4x A10G per-hour depending on provider and commitment. If we need predictable tail latency, reserved small pool is worth it; for bulk embedding batch jobs use a10g/spot. We should tag usage for cost center so finance can allocate.

Alex: Sounds good. Action items: 1) I created GCP quota ticket (ID: Q-11342) — infra-bot, can you link it? 2) Rashid to prepare CA flag patch + node pool recipe for prod H100 pool. 3) Sophie to validate NAT/egress so daemonsets can pull images. 4) Maria to validate fallback A10G sizing and cost delta.

infra-bot: Created ticket infra/GPU-EUW3-11342 and linked to Q-11342. Assigned to Rashid. :white_check_mark:

Rashid: I'll draft the node-pool recipe with taints/labels/ksa and post a short PR later today. Suggest minNodes=0, maxNodes=8 for burst, and 2-node dedicated pool for prod-critical with pre-provisioned images.

Alex: Awesome — please include the CA flags and priorityClass in the PR. Marking as blocker for the embed rollout until we have a dedicated minimal pool. :eyes:

Maria: +1 — also create a short playbook for runbook steps when CA flakes (check driver ds, node status, NAT).

Sophie: I'll run a quick egress check against the eu-west3 subnet and post results in this thread.

Alex: Thanks everyone.

(emoji reactions: :thumbsup: :rocket:)
